doc: A stale entry of the block collapsed (FBL 0.7, sections 8.1 and 8.5; DESL 0.2, section 5.5). lending.adp keeps ITEM-0002, ITEM-0003 and REQ-0001 collapsed, and its body, lending.md beside it (the same bytes as the body of the fixture one folder up), has no ITEM-0003: an agent deleted that item from the file while the designer was closed, and its number stays given, since the mark on line 2 names ITEM-0004. collapsed is declared with keys ids, so the entry whose key is no id of the model is stale: it is applied to no element, reported as fbl.stale-view-data, an information finding, at its line of the registration, line 4 (FBL 8.5, 15.3), and removed at the next write. The read shows what is collapsed when the document is opened again (FR-020): ITEM-0002 and REQ-0001, read from the registration as true, every other entry false.

attributes.title: A member borrows at most ten books at once.
A loan is renewed twice at most.
A reserved book is kept for a week.

steps.doc: The next write of the registration is a fold: the person collapses REQ-0003. Its entry goes where the ordinal order puts it among the entries that remain once the stale one is taken out, after REQ-0001 at the end of the block (FBL 8.4), and the stale ITEM-0003 is removed as part of the same edit, one remove-entry of its line (FBL 8.5). The block has history false, so the edit is no step of the history, and the removal of the stale entry is none either: no undo puts it back (FBL 8.5). The reading taken for the order of the two splices is the one fixtures/registration-blocks takes, the setting's own splice first, then the pruning; FBL 8.5 says only that the removal is part of the edit.
steps.expect:
etalii/hierarchical-requirement
collapsed:
  ITEM-0002: yes
  REQ-0001: yes
  REQ-0003: yes
